entries.title: Applying technology to understand and treat disease
entries.summary: A healthcare professional sits at a desk reviewing mammogram scans and medical diagrams on dual computer monitors.
entries.content:
Google’s health research and tools span from fundamental cellular discovery to laboratory analysis and patient impact. Over the last five years, Google teams have published 90 peer-reviewed research papers about understanding and addressing diseases, accumulating more than 90,000 citations. And building on our vision for how technology can accelerate science to improve lives, we’re collaborating with clinicians, academic institutes, and researchers to ensure discoveries make it out of the lab to benefit patients. Here is how our efforts are helping to advance medical research and public health solutions.

Decoding the mechanics of disease

AlphaGenome Atlas is the most comprehensive catalog of predictions for how single-letter variant changes in the human genome affect molecular biology.

To effectively treat an illness, it helps to understand how it operates at the molecular, genetic, and cellular levels. Our early-stage biology models act as collaborative research tools for scientists, revealing nature's hidden mechanics and advancing medical discoveries.

  • Accelerating drug discovery: Researchers at the Institute for Global Health, Barcelona, used AlphaFold to virtually screen 30,000 compounds for antiparasitic activity against Chagas disease, a neglected tropical illness that affects roughly 8 million people and can lead to life-threatening complications if left untreated. This research helped the Institute identify two FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed for Chagas, expediting time-to-treatment.
  • Mapping genetic variants linked to aging: Identifying which rare genetic changes are linked to specific diseases is challenging because the volume of non-impactful mutations creates "background noise." Researchers at the University of Exeter used AlphaGenome Atlas to search through genomic data from over 54,000 individuals, pinpointing specific variants that drive the abundance of critical proteins circulating in the human body, including PLA2G7 (linked to aging) and EGLN1 (a vital cellular oxygen sensor).
  • Reconstructing the brain at nanoscale: In partnership with Harvard’s Lichtman Lab, we reconstructed a human brain fragment at nanoscale resolution and made the data openly available via Neuroglancer. We additionally mapped the brains of model organisms including the fly, larval zebrafish, and songbird. These neural mapping resources enable researchers to advance their study of brain function.

Accelerating tools for medical solutions

Visual map of proteins developed with the support of AlphaFold.

The lab is where biological discovery is validated, engineered, and turned into potential medical and public health solutions. Our models have replaced slow, iterative processes with systems that can process large amounts of data quickly and accurately.

  • Supporting genetic diagnoses with ultrarapid genome sequencing: In collaboration with Stanford University School of Medicine, we used DeepVariant and DeepConsensus in a clinical trial to help determine the cause of genetic disease in time-critical cases. The program assisted in enabling life-saving interventions by achieving genetic diagnosis with whole genome sequencing in less than eight hours, an unprecedented achievement also recognized with a Guinness World Record.
  • Designing custom enzymes from scratch: We introduced AlphaProtein Novo, a machine learning pipeline for creating new-to-nature enzymes from first principles. In lab tests, it successfully designed custom enzymes to synthesize key drug motifs, and others to degrade toxic environmental plastics under extreme conditions — demonstrating the ability to design functional proteins that can go beyond what is currently known in nature.
  • Supporting proactive public health initiatives: A community's health is deeply connected to its geography. We are using our Google Earth AI models in combination with environmental, weather, mobility, and other data to help public health leaders forecast disease outbreaks and deliver care to vulnerable communities. In new research from WHO AFRO and the DRC’s INRB, conversational geospatial models replaced weeks of manual coding to help identify Ebola exposure and transmission risks sooner — allowing local responders to proactively deploy mobile laboratories.

Supporting medical providers with machine learning models

New mammography screening systems can help to catch historically missed interval cancers and reduce specialist reading workloads.

A medical breakthrough only matters if it can help real people. Our research demonstrates that machine learning models can help support disease detection as well as alleviate the administrative workload so providers can focus on care.

  • Flagging historically missed cancer signatures: In a pair of studies published in Nature Cancer in collaboration with Imperial College London and the UK’s National Health Service (NHS), we evaluated a mammography screening system across 125,000 women. The system caught 25% of historically missed interval cancers while showing the possibility of reducing specialist reading workloads by up to 40% — which could help provide crucial relief to healthcare systems facing severe radiologist shortages.
  • Uncovering hidden pediatric leukemia mutations: When applied by Children’s Mercy Hospital to previously sequenced real-world childhood leukemia cases, DeepSomatic confirmed all known variants while detecting 10 previously missed mutations — despite the challenge of working with a tumor-only sample. DeepSomatic is publicly available and has the potential to inform clinical judgments around patient risk and targeted treatments.
  • Predicting global flu surges: A Google flu forecasting model was ranked #1 by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) for predicting flu-related hospital admissions during the 2025–2026 season. Developed using our Empirical Research Assistance tool, the model outperformed 38 other systems to accurately match observed hospitalizations, showing how the technology can help public health officials anticipate demand for medical services and better prepare for seasonal outbreaks.

Better health within reach for everyone

Transforming health requires scientists, researchers, and institutions working hand-in-hand. That’s why we equip the science community with the advanced models and open-access platforms to fuel breakthrough research — along with the philanthropic funding and computing power they need to apply that research.

Through Google.org, we’re supporting organizations like the Infectious Disease Institute at Makerere University to forecast malaria drug resistance mutations with AlphaFold and AlphaMissense, and the University of Pennsylvania, using AlphaProteo and AlphaFold to help design novel cellular therapies that can augment the treatment of solid tumors and complex diseases. In 2026, Google.org has provided over $60 million to organizations around the world that are applying advanced models to transform how we understand and treat diseases.

By meeting disease at every stage, we can turn the most intractable human health challenges into actionable solutions, helping people everywhere live longer, healthier lives.

entries.title: Google Health: Evolving so you can focus on living better
entries.summary: What’s new from Google Health: Explore the new Fitbit Edge, expanded workout tracking, and dedicated women's health insights.
entries.content:
When we introduced the new Google Health app, Health Coach, and Fitbit Air just a few months ago, we set out on an ambitious journey: to shift health technology from a fragmented, reactive data-tracking ecosystem to a proactive, personalized companion for your everyday life.

The response has been incredible, with Fitbit Air capturing new users’ attention and drawing new audiences into Google Health. But that was just the beginning. We knew we’d need to continuously improve and innovate to make our app and personalized coaching as meaningful and helpful as possible. Over the past few months, we’ve focused on listening closely to feedback, relentlessly iterating with 10 releases and 55 feature updates to make our experiences better over time.

We know that true progress happens in the rhythm of daily life: meeting you where you are, adapting to your routine, and continuously improving. Today, we’re taking our next step forward across our devices, software, and ecosystem.

Introducing Google Fitbit Edge: A deliberate step change in design and performance. Sitting between the lightweight simplicity of Fitbit Air and the power of Pixel Watch 5, Fitbit Edge is built for active lifestyles, offering glanceable, real-time guidance and serving as an on-wrist window to the Google Health Coach.

Improving Fitbit Air: From bringing passive cardiometabolic trend tracking with Health Guardian features to innovating our activity detection accuracy for 100+ workouts, we're making our tracker experiences smarter, more proactive, and deeply integrated across our platform to do the thinking so you don’t have to. New Metal Mesh Fitbit Air bands expand the styling possibilities, transforming your everyday tracker into elegant jewelry.

Making a leap forward for women’s health: Recognizing that health looks different across every body and life stage, we’re partnering with Flo Health — the world’s leading female health app — to integrate deeply important cycle, pregnancy, and menopause guidance directly into our app and Coach, alongside groundbreaking research in this underserved and often-generalized population.

Welcoming world-class talent to Google Health: We’re welcoming exceptional new leaders, researchers, and builders to join Performance Advisor Stephen Curry on the Google Health team to accelerate our mission and push the boundaries of what health technology can do.

Health is complex, personal, and deeply human. We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to showing up every day, learning from you, and continuously refining our tools to help you live a longer, healthier life.

entries.title: From game days to daily life: The familiar faces teaming up with Google Health
entries.content:
Listen to article This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental

We’ve teamed up with some of the most accomplished athletes, creators, and wellness experts to help shape the new Google Health experience. From an NBA champion and an Olympic heptathlete to a registered dietitian and a YouTube creator, here’s a look at how this dynamic group is putting Google Health app, Google Health Coach, and Fitbit wearables to work in their daily lives. Plus, how their feedback makes our health technology more intuitive, personalized, and helpful for everyone.

The game changers

  • Stephen Curry: As our official Performance Advisor for Google Health, Stephen brings his natural tech curiosity straight to our product teams. Stephen and his trainers work hands-on with our engineers to test coaching built with Gemini with live biometric data, co-design hardware, and turn complex athletic insights into simple tips for daily life.
  • Bryson DeChambeau: Known for his obsession with biomechanics, Bryson pairs his analytical mindset with our health teams. He inputs his off-course training, rest, and energy burn metrics into Google’s algorithms to help fine-tune personalized Google Health Coach insights.
  • JuJu Watkins: JuJu balances college classes, brand commitments, community foundations, and team ownership with Boston Legacy FC. As she works her way back on the court post injury, JuJu is using Google Health Coach to keep her sleep, nutrition, and recovery steady even with an unpredictable schedule.
  • Chari Hawkins: For an Olympic heptathlete, precision is everything. Chari uses Google Health Coach to monitor her fitness, recovery, and women's health insights, showing how everyday athletes can use the same data-driven tools to hit their own goals.
  • Sophia Wilson: Juggling life as a pro soccer player for the Portland Thorns FC and the U.S. women's national soccer team, plus life with a toddler, Sophia relies on Google Health Coach to keep tabs on her nutrition and log her meals as she navigates returning to the pitch.

The culture shapers

  • Alex Cooper: Through her Unwell network, Alex brings candid conversations to millions every week. Now, she is teaming up with Google Health to show how tools like Google Health Coach can help her community build sustainable daily routines, prioritize recovery, and hit their wellness goals. Alex also works with our teams to weave products like Pixel, Gemini, and Google Cloud into her workflow, making health and tech feel approachable and fun.
  • MrBeast: MrBeast is adopting Google Health tools as his go-to resources for fitness and recovery. He is weaving the Google Health Coach into his challenges, most recently his Grocery store challenge, and collaborating with our team on an exciting new initiative launching next year.

The daily motivators

  • Jess Sims: The Peloton instructor is bringing her "You don't have to, you get to" philosophy to help users build balanced, sustainable routines. With an emphasis on progress over perfection, she shows how Fitbit and Google Health Coach connect the dots across sleep, cycle phases, and recovery to help everyone feel their best.
  • Kylie Sakaida: The NYT best-selling cookbook author and registered dietitian uses Google Health app and Google Health Coach to share stress-free nutrition tips, proving wellness tools are built for everyday meals, not just elite training plans.

Whether you are training for a championship or simply trying to get an extra hour of sleep, Google Health is built to help you build habits that fit your life.

entries.title: We’re partnering with Flo Health to elevate women’s health
entries.content:
A truly personalized health experience starts with understanding the unique rhythms of your body. With Google Health Coach, 1 we’re building a personal health experience that adapts to your lifestyle, habits, and biology — which is especially important for women. Connecting the dots across sleep, daily readiness, activity, and recovery gives a clearer picture of your overall health across the different phases of your cycle and stages of life. That is why we make it easy to log your cycle dates and symptoms, or quickly view period predictions and cycle phases — either on-wrist with Fitbit Edge or in the Google Health app. And with Google Health Premium, you can receive tailored, cycle-aware coaching, too. 2

As part of our long-term commitment to invest in and support women's health, we’re launching a landmark, multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health, the world's leading female health platform used by more than 80 million women every month. This collaboration will help build a cohesive, empowering experience to manage daily health. Plus, we'll partner on initiatives that further women's health.

A multi-year vision for tailored guidance

Because your body goes through complex phases throughout the month and major shifts throughout life, health insights must continuously adapt. Google Health aims to give you a complete view of your overall wellbeing across all phases and stages of life — from periods to pregnancy to perimenopause. When you wear a smartwatch or tracker 24/7, like the Google Fitbit Air , Pixel Watch 5, or all new Google Fitbit Edge, you capture the continuous, night-over-night biometric data needed to truly understand these shifts.

Our collaboration with Flo Health will focus on four central pillars:

  • Secure, consent-based app syncing: Beginning early next year, you will be able to easily sync your Flo Health app with Google Health. With your consent, your cycle data from Flo Health can be linked with your Google Health metrics (e.g. resting heart rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, and sleep stages) to give you one clear picture of your day. Similarly, the data from your Google Health app will be made available to Flo for a deeper, more personalized, and consistent experience between apps.
  • Google Health Coach integration: 3 Flo Health data will integrate with your Google Health Coach. Whether you’re navigating cycle health or managing perimenopause, with Google Health Premium your coach will connect the dots across your cycle, sleep, and recovery to give you tailored, actionable guidance.
  • Ground-breaking women’s health research: We plan to partner on dedicated research initiatives spanning underserved topics — this may include perimenopause, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), pregnancy, and postpartum recovery.
  • New products: We will partner to build new products that are specifically designed for women, with a deep integration of Flo's women's health insights and algorithms with our expertise in wearable hardware and advanced sensors.

Built with uncompromising privacy and expertise

We recognize that women’s health data is deeply personal. Your trust is our top priority, which is why this entire experience is built on a strict, transparent opt-in model.

Flo Health and Google Health are committed to data privacy and security, and a crucial part of this partnership is ensuring women stay in control. No data will move between the apps without your explicit permission — given separately for each type of data and each purpose — and you have the control to withdraw permission at any time. Flo data shared with Google Health will never be used for advertising, never be sold, and will not be made available to other apps or developers through Google's health platforms.

We are eager to bring thoughtful, innovative experiences to women at every stage of their health journey. This is just the beginning of a long-term partnership to make personalized health guidance a daily reality.

entries.title: How we’re making Google Health and Fitbit Air smarter than ever
entries.summary: The photo shows Fitbit Air with a Metal Mesh band.
entries.content:
Since introducing the Google Health app and Google Health Coach, 1 we've consistently delivered new features (more than 55 of them!) and fixes based on your feedback. We've added more customization to your Today tab, expanded focus metrics, improved Coach memory, deepened our Apple Health™ 2 integration, made it easy to log meals with a quick photo or chat with your Coach, and so much more.

We've also expanded our roster of fitness wearables: first with our screenless tracker, Fitbit Air 3 — introducing a playful, fan-favorite Pokémon™ 4 Sleep Special Edition — and then with our most advanced wearable, Pixel Watch 5, which brings proactive assistance and advanced health tracking to your wrist. And now, we are bringing you the new Fitbit Edge, 5 our next-generation tracker with advanced fitness and real-time guidance at a glance.

To help you get the most out of this growing lineup — and to deliver on our commitment to make the Google Health app and Health Coach better over time — we’re pairing these wearables with new premium accessories, industry-leading partnerships, and powerful, advanced health and wellness tools that work quietly in the background.

Elevate your look with the Metal Mesh bands.

Turn your tracker into a piece of jewelry designed to be worn day to night. The new Fitbit Air Metal Mesh band is crafted from a flexible, stainless steel weave that drapes elegantly around your wrist to deliver a contemporary, chic, upscale look for tracking you’ll definitely want to take out on the town. Pre-order a lightweight, easy-to-wear Metal Mesh band in Champagne Gold or Polished Silver for $69.99. Or get the Champagne Gold Metal Mesh band with an Obsidian Fitbit Air for $149.99 exclusively at Target and on the Google Store.

Monitor your well-being with Health Guardian.

Health Guardian features — our new suite of health and safety tools that track subtle changes to your health over time — are rolling out to Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge for users with a Google Health Premium subscription later this month. Set up blood pressure trends and insulin resistance trends 6 in the Google Health app, and if you meet the monthly wear requirements, you'll get a report at the beginning of each month to help you make lifestyle adjustments early. With Google Health Premium, your Coach can help you translate any shifts in patterns, adapt your fitness plan, and give you personalized lifestyle and wellness guidance — plus, additional context to share with your doctor.

Track your workouts with upgraded automatic activity detection.

Based on your feedback, we improved automatic activity tracking so it’s more intelligent, accurate, and reliable. By automatically logging your workouts, even when you forget, it helps you stay focused on your workout rather than your screen. This experience is available across Fitbit Air, Fitbit Edge, and Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 later this month.

It’s broader and more accurate than ever.

  • Tracks more activities: We expanded the number of activities your Fitbit tracker or Pixel Watch can detect from 10 to more than 100, including strength training, swimming, and racket and team sports.
  • Uses more context: Powered by contextual reasoning, Google Health factors in critical context — including your workout routines, historical data, manual edits, and, with permission, your location — to deliver nearly 2x more accurate detections and cut missed workouts by more than half. 7
  • Logs workouts automatically: Workouts that meet your minimum duration threshold (15 minutes by default) with a sustained elevated heart rate are automatically logged, and a summary is sent to your mobile app, typically within 30 minutes.
  • Learns your patterns: When you confirm or edit an activity, you’re improving a feature that learns your unique patterns and uses them to refine its predictions.

This marks a huge advancement for automatic tracking, and we will keep working to make it even better.

Tap into a growing network of app partners.

We’re committed to helping you bring together your health data through industry-leading partnerships and a safe, secure, and private platform.

  • Connect cycle data with Flo Health: Through our multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health, beginning early next year, you’ll be able to sync your Flo Health app directly with Google Health to receive deeper, personalized insights tailored to your cycle phase and life stage. Together, we’re also advancing clinical research into women's health to better support women everywhere.
  • See your glucose trends in one view with Abbott: 8 Through our recently announced partnership with Abbott, users in the U.S. will soon be able to connect Abbott’s Lingo™ 9 over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor to the Google Health app for deeper, unified insights across glucose, meals, workouts, and sleep. More capabilities will roll out soon.
  • Sync nutrition with MyFitnessPal: Our expanded integration with MyFitnessPal makes it easy to bring your daily meal and nutrition logs from MyFitnessPal into Google Health. This update allows MyFitnessPal Premium users to share their more detailed, food-specific logs with the Google Health app; non-premium users can continue to share daily meal logs.
  • Get lab insights with Function Health: To get an even more complete picture of your overall well-being, users in the U.S. will also be able to import clinical lab results from Function Health starting later this fall.

With upgraded features, new proactive health insights, and a growing network of partner integrations, we’re putting the tools for a healthier, more active life directly in your hands.

entries.title: Google Fitbit Edge: Our all-new smartest fitness tracker ever
entries.content:
Whether you’re training for a race, balancing a packed schedule, or building sustainable wellness habits, staying motivated is easier when you have the right companion on your wrist. We first introduced the Google Health Coach 1 across our smartwatch lineup with Pixel Watch and lightweight, screenless wearables like Fitbit Air. Now, we’re bringing that intelligent, personalized coaching experience to our most focused, ultra-slim glanceable device yet: Google Fitbit Edge, 2 our next-generation fitness tracker designed for active lifestyles and everyday wear.

Many people are looking for a wearable that sits between an advanced smartwatch like Pixel Watch and the quiet simplicity of a band like Fitbit Air. That’s Fitbit Edge. It's small and comfortable but also a powerful daily companion that's designed to help you reach your wellness goals. It combines Fitbit’s trusted health expertise with Google’s refined design and everyday helpfulness. Encased in durable recycled aluminum, 3 it features a slim, comfortable profile that naturally contours to your wrist. Despite the lightweight design, it delivers weekend-to-weekend battery life. 4

See more with a sleek display.

Even with a remarkably thin profile, it features our largest and brightest tracker screen yet, delivering 46% more viewing area than previous trackers and a vibrant display that’s easy to read even in direct sunlight. 5

Navigating your stats is intuitive with a brilliant Hybrid OLED display featuring glanceable tiles and expressive clock faces. We’ve also redesigned a physical side button to provide tactile feedback, giving you control to quickly take action, like pulling up the workout pause screen, without missing a beat.

All of this is displayed within a carefully crafted, reimagined design with a soft shape and elegant silhouette, which precisely follows the natural curve of your wrist. Measuring just 11.5mm thin and featuring a case that’s 45% lighter than the Apple Watch Series 12, Fitbit Edge is sleek and comfortable to wear all day and night.

Navigate quickly with a fluid interface.

Building on the intuitive experience introduced with Pixel Watch 5, our completely reimagined on-device interface puts everything you need right at your fingertips. Glanceable complications keep your essential stats front and center, from steps and weather to on-demand workouts, while fluid tiles bring rich Google Health metrics like sleep, cycle tracking, and heart rate directly to your wrist. It’s also packed with helpful everyday features, like Google Maps, media controls, and call and message notifications. With a versatile library of customizable watch faces and interchangeable bands, it’s tuned to your day, your health, and your style.

Train smarter with advanced fitness tools.

Fitbit Edge consolidates core athletic tracking tools into a unified, on-wrist experience that lets you evaluate your performance at a glance:

  • New workout views and real-time guidance: The exercise app lets you track more than 50 exercise modes to start right on your wrist, with glanceable real-time guidance to help you reach your goals. Whether you need core metrics for Pilates, pace targets to hit a new PR on your run, heart rate zones for HIIT intervals, or splits during track workouts, your stats are clear without breaking your stride.
  • Consolidated location and effort tracking: Built-in precision GPS delivers up to 40% improved tracking accuracy over previous generations, even without your phone. Its aluminum housing with nano-molded technology along with an upgraded GPS chipset enables this advancement in precise route mapping accuracy. And the integrated altimeter measures elevation changes during hill sprints, outdoor runs, or stair workouts, giving you an accurate picture of total physical output.
  • Intelligent, automatic activity tracking: Fitbit Edge automatically recognizes and categorizes up to 100 workouts, from outdoor runs and rides to daily walks, even if you forget to hit start. It’s powered by next-generation intelligence that analyzes the context of your activity to recognize what you did and count every bit of effort toward your weekly goals.

Track deeply with state-of-the-art health sensors.

Underneath its refined exterior, Fitbit Edge combines deep biometric insights powered by advanced sensor technology with intelligent health tracking to give you a complete picture of your well-being.

  • Health Guardian features: 6 Quietly tracks important shifts in your health and wellness in the background — including blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and high/low heart rate alerts 7 — to help you stay ahead of changes. With Google Health Premium, your Coach can help you translate shifts in patterns, give you personalized lifestyle and wellness guidance, adapt your fitness plan, and give you context for conversations with your doctor.
  • State-of-the-art sensing: Take heart rhythm assessments anytime using the on-wrist ECG app, 8 while continuous optical heart rate monitoring tracks rest and recovery trends around the clock.
  • Holistic overnight insights: The dedicated skin temperature sensor 9 tracks nightly fluctuations, complementing sleep stage analysis and HRV metrics 10 to deliver comprehensive recovery scoring each morning.

Go further with weekend-to-weekend battery life.

With up to seven days of battery life on a single charge, 11 you can track workouts by day and sleep stages by night with total peace of mind. When you need a quick top-up, fast magnetic charging delivers a full day of battery in just five minutes 12 when your battery is low.

Built with an elegant, protective metal housing and refined touchpoints, Fitbit Edge is water-resistant up to 50 meters 13 and ready for any workout. It’s also our first repairable fitness tracker, featuring an internal modular architecture and a replaceable battery designed to extend the life of your device.

Personalize your look with tailored style.

Fitbit Edge comes in four distinct finishes paired with our ultra-soft Active Bands: 14 Obsidian (Matte Black case), Fog (Polished Silver case), Olive (Satin Pyrite case), and Canyon (Warm Gold case).

Personalize your look with a full line of interchangeable accessories, including breathable Active Sport band, micro-adjustable Performance Loop band, 15 sleek Magnet band, and the elevated Metal Links band.

Additionally, we’re launching a Stephen Curry Special Edition Fitbit Edge, created alongside four-time NBA Champion and Google Performance Advisor Stephen Curry. Water-repellent 16 and moisture-wicking, it features his signature rye tones and game day orange, available for $219.99.

Google Fitbit Edge, which retails for $179.99, is now available for pre-order on the Google Store and through retail partners. It will be on shelves October 27. You’ll get three months of Google Health Premium on us when you purchase Google Fitbit Edge.

entries.title: Study in The Lancet suggests AI could improve patient-physician relationships.
entries.summary: A peer-reviewed study in The Lancet evaluates Google's AMIE medical AI in a real-world primary care clinic.
entries.content:
Can AI safely assess patients’ needs before they step into a doctor’s office? A study led by researchers at Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) and published in The Lancet today, offers an encouraging first look. As Google’s first-ever publication in the main journal of The Lancet, this research marks a significant milestone.

In a real-world clinical study at BIDMC’s ambulatory primary care clinic, 98 patients consulted AMIE, our research diagnostic AI chatbot, ahead of urgent care visits. Supervising physicians monitored the interactions in real time, and not a single conversation needed to be interrupted based on predefined safety criteria. And clinicians reported that the AI summaries helped them prepare for visits in 75% of cases and influenced their approach to care in more than half. AMIE’s differential diagnoses also matched the doctors’ final diagnoses 90% of the time.

While larger clinical trials are needed to assess patient-facing AI at scale, the findings suggest the potential for AI to enhance the patient-physician relationship and ease the strain on healthcare workers. And they demonstrate meaningful progress as we push the boundaries of what’s possible for AI in science and health. Read the complete research paper in The Lancet.

entries.title: Sign in quickly and securely with passkeys.
entries.summary: Learn how to set up a passkey for your Google Account.
entries.content:
This Cybersecurity Awareness Month, make signing in easier and more secure with passkeys.

Passkeys let you sign in to apps or sites the same way you unlock your device: with a fingerprint, face scan, or device PIN code, making them easier and more secure than passwords. (Biometric data like your fingerprint or face scan stays on your device and is never shared with Google.) And, unlike passwords, passkeys are designed to be resistant to common online attacks like phishing.

Ready to make the switch? To set up a passkey for your Google Account, visit g.co/passkeys, click “Create a passkey,” and follow the prompts.

entries.title: Google Cloud introduces the Gemini agent.
entries.summary: Google Cloud’s new Gemini agent automates workflows by connecting to your business systems. See how it streamlines enterprise tasks in one prompt.
entries.content:
Today at Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud announced the Gemini agent, a universal agent for work.

With Gemini, work now starts in the prompt window:

  • Gemini has all of an organization’s business context and can be used for everything from knowledge work to answering questions, and content creation to coding, all from a single prompt box.
  • It plans the work, uses skills and tools, connects to Cloud customers’ business systems, and brings back something finished — inside the documents, the inbox, and the developer environments they already work in.
  • It chooses the best model for the job, has built-in cost controls, and most importantly, has the security, administration, and governance required by enterprise customers.

Check out the Google Cloud blog to learn more.
